app:F1.title: After the buffer folder changes, recordings kept in the old folder are never recovered
app:F1.problem: _startupBufferFolder is set from the current setting at launch (line 206), and RecoverKeptRecordingsAsync scans only that root (line 842). CleanupStaleBufferAsync also cleans only the current root. When a recording can't be saved, the engine keeps it with its recovery note in the session folder under the buffer root that was active then (TearDownSessionAsync, then RescuePendingRecordingsAsync). Once the user points the buffer folder somewhere else, that old root is never scanned again. Meanwhile the UI tells the user three times that the recording 'is saved the next time PC Clipper starts': the ApplySettingsAsync confirm text (line 2151), the kept-recording banner, and the engine notice.
app:F1.scenario: The buffer drive C: fills up during a long recording. The engine's 'drive is almost full' stop tries to save the recording, the save fails, and the recording is kept as pending. The user turns replay off (StopAsync keeps it, with its note, in C:\...\Buffer\session_x), or presses Apply on the restart prompt, which says it 'saves it the next time PC Clipper starts'. They then follow the app's own advice ('pick another drive in Settings') and set the buffer folder to D:\Buffer. On the next launch _startupBufferFolder is D:\Buffer, so the recording in C: is never recovered or reported. Its multi-GB session folder also stays on C: forever, on the drive that was already full.
app:F1.verified_fix: 1) Add a persisted `List<string> KeptRecordingRoots` to AppSettings (Normalize: distinct full paths, case-insensitive). 2) Add a root to it: in OnEngineNotice when the 'will try again next time it starts (<dir>)' notice arrives (root = Path.GetDirectoryName(dir)), or better have the engine expose the kept session's BufferRoot. Also add it in ApplySettingsAsync when old.BufferFolder != next.BufferFolder and (PendingCount()>0 or FindKeptRecordingNotes(old.BufferFolder).Count>0). Save settings right away. 3) RecoverKeptRecordingsAsync: loop over the distinct set {_startupBufferFolder} ∪ KeptRecordingRoots captured at startup. Call ReplayEngine.RecoverKeptRecordingsAsync per root, combine the results and the `left` notes for the banner, and drop a root from the list (then SaveSettings) once FindKeptRecordingNotes(root) is empty. Optionally run SegmentStore.CleanupStaleSessions on it too. 4) Until then, the line-2151 and line-588 texts and the ToggleReplay confirm should not promise automatic recovery when the buffer folder is being changed.

app:F2.title: Changing the buffer folder after a fault, then Turn ON, silently deletes footage the app says can still be saved
app:F2.problem: ConfirmNewBufferFormat decides whether to warn by comparing only CaptureConfig.Signature (encoder, size, fps, audio; Models.cs:117). The buffer root is not part of it. ApplySettingsAsync shows no 'buffer is cleared' prompt for a faulted buffer either, because ReplayWanted is false once _wantReplayOn was cleared by a non-retryable fault (line 2142). StartReplayAsync then calls StartAsync(keepBuffer: true), and the engine sees session.BufferRoot != cfg.BufferRoot, so it finishes any recording and runs TearDownSessionAsync. That deletes the session directory holding the still-saveable buffer, with no question asked.
app:F2.scenario: In a game the janitor stops the replay with 'Drive C:\ is almost full ... Free up space or pick another drive in Settings' (FaultNotRetryable). Home shows 'Replay stopped: ... What was recorded before that can still be saved.' The user opens Settings, sets the buffer folder to D:\ and presses Save, and no restart warning appears (not active). They press Turn ON. ConfirmNewBufferFormat sees the same signature and returns true without a dialog, the engine tears down the C: session, and the last 15 minutes they meant to save are gone. A controller or hotkey toggle (StartKind.Hotkey) does the same without even the format check.
app:F2.verified_fix: In ConfirmNewBufferFormat, compute rootChanged with the engine's own rule: `Path.GetFullPath(previous.BufferRoot) != Path.GetFullPath(next.BufferRoot)`. The engine compares ordinal (case-sensitive) against session.BufferRoot, so match that exactly, or better expose ReplayEngine's session BufferRoot and compare to that. Return true only when `next.Signature == previous.Signature && !rootChanged`. Otherwise ask, with text that names the folder change ('You changed the buffer folder, so turning the replay on starts a new buffer there and the X min still held can't be saved after that'). In ApplySettingsAsync, when BufferFolder changes and `_engine.State == EngineState.Faulted && CanSave`, also show a confirm (suggest saving a clip first). For StartKind.Hotkey after a fault where the root or signature changed and SafeBuffered()>0, don't discard silently: refuse with a toast ('Open PC Clipper to turn the replay on - the buffer from before can still be saved'), or require the window.

app:F5.title: Xbox-button (Guide) presets open Xbox Game Bar or the Steam overlay, so the game loses focus every time the shortcut is used
app:F5.problem: FillPadBox offers every PadChord.Preset, including Guide+A, Guide+X and Guide+Y (Core Controller.cs:68), as ordinary choices. On Windows 10/11, 'Open Xbox Game Bar using this button on a controller' is on by default, so pressing the Xbox button opens Game Bar over the game and takes input focus. With Steam running, the PS or Xbox button also brings Steam to the front. This defeats the feature's purpose ('Works while you play, also in fullscreen games') and the never-take-focus rule the hotkey and toast code goes to great lengths to keep.
app:F5.scenario: The user picks 'Xbox button + A' for 'Save the replay' in Settings. In a fullscreen game they hold the Xbox button and press A. The clip saves, but Game Bar opens on the Guide press and becomes the foreground window, so the game stops receiving input. A game in exclusive fullscreen may minimize.
app:F5.verified_fix: Lowest-risk fix: remove the three `Of(PadButtons.Guide, ...)` entries from PadChord.Presets. FillPadBox already appends any saved non-preset chord as its own item, so existing Guide bindings keep working and stay visible. No tests reference Presets or Guide. Alternative: keep them but label them in FillPadBox, e.g. DescribeBoth + ' - may open Xbox Game Bar (turn that off in Windows Settings > Gaming > Xbox Game Bar)', and add the same caveat to the padNote text.

controller-input:ctl-bt-ghost-connected.title: A paired Bluetooth PlayStation pad that is switched off is reported as connected and never as disconnected
controller-input:ctl-bt-ghost-connected.problem: A non-dongle pad is announced (sink.OnPadConnected) as soon as its HID path opens, before any input report has arrived. Nothing ever times it out either: a pad is closed only when a read fails or its path leaves the SetupDi list. Windows keeps the HID interface of a paired classic-Bluetooth device present after the device disconnects. CreateFile still succeeds and reads just stay pending; Dolphin's IOWin.cpp documents this ('Even minutes after a disconnect, CreateFile will succeed and reads will just time out'). SDL handles it by treating the device as connected only while packets arrive (500 ms silence, then a probe write). This code never writes to the pad, so Windows never notices that it is gone. The report offsets, CRC check, P/Invoke layouts and overlapped-read lifetime all checked out against hid-playstation.c, SDL_hidapi_ps4.c and SDL_hidapi_ps5.c; this is the one wrong-state behaviour in the lens.
controller-input:ctl-bt-ghost-connected.scenario: A DualSense is paired over Bluetooth but switched off, and PC Clipper autostarts at login. Rescan finds the path, the probe and the GENERIC_READ open both succeed, and OnPadConnected fires. The user gets the toast 'PS5 controller connected - Create/Share + Cross saves the last 15 min' on every login, and Settings > Controller lists 'DualSense Wireless Controller - Bluetooth' as connected while the pad is off. Likewise, a pad switched off mid-session (with no Steam running to send SDL's probe write) is never reported disconnected, so the list stays wrong until restart. Shortcuts do still work once the pad is on, because reports resume on the same handle.
controller-input:ctl-bt-ghost-connected.verified_fix: In TryOpen (lines 169-174), stop announcing non-dongle pads; leave Announced = false. In OnReport, after the checksum filter and before line 288, add: `if (!pad.IsDongle && !pad.Announced) { pad.Announced = true; sink.OnPadConnected(pad.Info); }`. Record a timestamp for every accepted report in a new field, e.g. pad.LastReportMs = Environment.TickCount64, or pass nowMs into the handler. USB pads stream at 250-1000 Hz, so they are announced within a poll or two. Leave the dongle path as it is. Optional silence timeout: in Poll, after the Pump loop, do `if (pad.BluetoothPath && !pad.IsDongle && pad.Announced && nowMs - pad.LastReportMs > 5000) { pad.Announced = false; sink.OnPadDisconnected(pad.Info); }`. Keep the handle and reader open so the next report announces the pad again. Do not dispose the pad, and do not touch _backoff, which is keyed off OpenedAtMs. Apply this timeout only to pads known to stream continuously, e.g. pad.ValidChecksums > 0 (genuine pads sending full CRC reports). Otherwise skip it or use a much longer timeout. SDL notes that the 8BitDo Zero 2, a PS4 clone, only sends reports when its state changes, and a short timeout would make such pads flap between connected and disconnected in the log and the list. The toast fires once per controller per session, so re-announcing will not spam toasts. Close() already sends OnPadDisconnected only when Announced is true, so it stays correct. Update any test that expects a connect event on open.

controller-input:ctl-exclusive-ds4window.title: PC Clipper's always-open shared handle makes DS4Windows' exclusive mode fail, so games see the pad twice
controller-input:ctl-exclusive-ds4window.problem: Every supported Sony pad is kept open with a GENERIC_READ handle for as long as PC Clipper runs. An exclusive open (share mode 0) by another program is then refused with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION. DS4Windows' 'Hide DS4 Controller' option (exclusive mode, the older alternative to HidHide) depends on that open. When it fails, a non-elevated DS4Windows falls back to shared mode and the real pad stays visible to games next to the virtual Xbox pad. The class remarks mention this only as a caveat; the README and the Settings hint do not.
controller-input:ctl-exclusive-ds4window.scenario: PC Clipper (autostart) opens the DualShock 4 at login, then DS4Windows starts with 'Hide DS4 Controller' on and without admin rights. Its exclusive CreateFile fails, so it opens the pad shared. The game now reads the DS4 through DirectInput or SDL and the ViGEm Xbox pad at the same time, which gives doubled or conflicting inputs in-game. Users without PC Clipper have no such problem.
controller-input:ctl-exclusive-ds4window.verified_fix: Minimum: add a line to README.md (Controller section, next to the Steam/DS4Windows note at line 52) and to the Settings > Controller hint. Wording: 'If you use DS4Windows, hide the controller with HidHide (and add PC Clipper to HidHide's allowed apps, or leave it out and PC Clipper will use DS4Windows' virtual Xbox pad). DS4Windows' old Hide DS4 Controller (exclusive) option can't work while PC Clipper or Steam has the controller open.' Optional: add a setting such as 'Read PlayStation controllers directly' (default on) that keeps SonyHidPads from opening pads. Do not use the suggested automatic skip-on-DS4Windows.exe as written. With DS4Windows in DS4-emulation output mode and HidHide hiding the real pad, the ViGEm virtual DS4 (054C:05C4) is a Sony HID device that only SonyHidPads can read, so skipping all Sony paths would turn controller shortcuts off completely. If automation is wanted, release only non-virtual pads: walk the parent devnodes with CM_Get_Parent and exempt anything under ViGEmBus. Also expect a UAC prompt from DS4Windows if PC Clipper grabs the pad first.
